latin.619: §. XXIV. Probatum sic ad oculum est, præsentiam corporis & sanguinis Christi in Cœna veram & realissimam, i. e. Spiritualem, à Reformata Ecclesia edoctam semper esse atque hodienum edoceri, ab ipso Cœnæ Sacræ Institutore Christo, per omnem seculorum Christianorum decursum, uti in aliis Ecclesiis sotam conservatamque, sic ad Ecclesiam Reformatam successionis ordine, derivatam; quam insuper, Fidei, seu manducationi spirituali antecedaneam, cum COSINO Episcopo Dunelmensi ipsimet professi sumus in Tractatulo Germanico Kurzer Entwurff. p. 64.
latin.620: Cæterùm assertionis hujus veritas ac evidentia, Reformatorum testimoniis quàm plurimis firmata ac stabilita, adeo nuper perstrinxit cujusdam Professoris Clarissimi oculos, ut in Disputatione publica de Cœna, superiori anno cameraliter ab eo habitâ, quò fundamentalem in hoc articulo Protestantium Dissensum, deplorando certè conatu, evinceret, verba Reformatorum Confessionesque externas, Fidei ipsorum non congruere, h. e. ut verbis ejus utar; Reformatos reverà id non credere quod se credere simulant, neminique non constare, aliud illos sentire, aliud loqui, haud verecundatus fuerit scribere §. 3. Cui gravissimæ injuriæ, toti Ecclesiæ Reformatæ adeo iniquè, & ob finem tam tetrum invidiosumque illatæ, nihil aliud reponimus, quàm fidi Præceptoris sui, Joh. Conr. Danhaueri verba, quibus Waldensium causam, in isto eodem casu, contra Joh. Marianam aliosque Pontificios, defendit, citra tamen omnem, ad Personam Professoris applicationem à nobis recitanda: Adhuc nostro, inquit, seculo, ausi sunt Pontificii scribere, statuisse Waldenses, in Eucharistia sacramento corpus Christi non esse. Colorem rei faciunt per aliam calumniam, quam ipsi Waldenses recensent in Responsione excusatoria ad Literas Augustin. pag. 87. Falso nos arguunt, non esse hanc nostram Confessionem, ex ejusmodi ratione, quod alia scribimus de Sacramento Corporis Christi, & alia credimus. Quibus ita præmissis, subjicit Danhauerus id, quod ab hoc loco alienum non est: Hoc nim. ultimum effugium est eorum, qui si aliàs resorbere calumnias cogerentur, hypocriseos adversarium sine ratione postulant; Dissert. de Ecclesia Waldensium. art. 4. Phænom. 10. §. 34. in medio.
latin.621: Quæ Vir Clarissimus ad speciem quandam injuriæ, Reformatorum Cætui factæ, conciliandam, de intentionali & effectiva corporis Christi in S. Cœna præsentia, nonnullis Reformatis memorata; ab aliis corporis Christi agnita sinceréque professa à S. Cœna absentia; §. eodem 4tio; Quartò verò sphæra distantia Corporis Christi à Cœna S. tanta, quanta altissimum Cœlum à terra distat, ex Calvino, deque tàm illocali, quam locali Christi præsentia in Cœna neganda, §. 5. ex Trelcatio adducit, præterquam quòd (1) privatorum sensuque suo abundantium Auctorum Commenta sunt, pleraque contra mentem eorum detorta, quasi ista omni reali corporis Christi in S. Cœna præsentiæ opposita essent, quod tamen secus se habere ex testimoniis eorum, in Tractatulo meo adscriptis, in propatulo est: Certè, non magis Reformatam Ecclesiam ista feriunt (etiam si detorta non essent, humani potiùs aliquid passa sibi que ipsis adversa) quam Ecclesiam, solam Auctori orthodoxam vereque Lutheranàm habitam, ferire videbuntur asserta quorundam vel Pietistarum, vel Syncretistarum nomine vulgò venientium, speciatim Calixti, cujus Autoritatem exigui inter orthodoxos momenti esse Autor perhibet §. 20. ut qui non modò cum Reformatis, sed etiam cum Pontificiis, colluserit, de Symbolis Ecclesiarum Lutheranarum secùs judicaverit, & nonnullos ad deserendam veritatem adduxerit.
latin.622: Etiam (2) Non omnia in Autoribus leguntur quæ in iis exstare innuit Vir Clarissimus, exempli gratiâ, in Trelcatio: Nec locali, nec illocali modo corpus Christi in terra præsens esse, haud exstat, quandoquidem Trelcatii verba ita sonant; Cùm enim Christi corpus, nostro homoousion, in Cœlo, ubicunque vult, circumscriptivè sit, (puta ex natura corporis, quòd in loco, i.e. alio corpore, non potest aliter, quam circumscriptive adesse) non per modum invisibilem, incircumscriptum, (puta vel absolutè & simpliciter talem, seu infinitum (qui solius Dei est) vel indefinitum, (seu definitivum, Angelis à Scholasticis essentialem habitum) qui modi omnes & singuli veritatem corporis evertunt (utpote vel DEO, vel Angelis proprii & essentiales adæquatè) omnino Christum corporaliter in Cœlo, Corpore tamen in Cœna, modo sacramentali, i. e. spirituali, adesse fatendum est. pag. m. 185. 186.; Etiam (3) quicquid vel de intentionali, vel effectiva Corporis Christi in Cœna præsentia Auctorum nonnulli; vel alii de distantia Corporis Christi à Cœna, haud minori, quàm quæ Cœlum inter & terram obtinet; vel pars de ipsâ absentiâ Corporis Christi à Cœna; vel denique Trelcatius, de tàm affirmato circumscriptivo in cœlis Corporis Christi præsentiæ modo, quam negato incircumscriptivo in terris adessendi ejusdem modo, tradunt, id omne soli corporali, locali, crassóque Corporis Christi, vel in, vel cum, vel sub pane Eucharistiæ adessendi modo oppositum cupiunt: Nam, inquit Trelcatius; Cordibus eorum re verâ præsens Christus est, iis, qui credunt, eâdem omnino præsentiâ qualis & Communio Corporis sui ipsis exhibetur in Cœna. Atque hæc præsentia REALIS est, neutra tamen præsentia CORPORALIS. Nam fide, ut ait Ambrosius, tangitur Christus, non Corpore. Edit. Leidens. pag 184. in medio. Et paucis intersertis: Modus, ait, præsentiæ Corporis Christi in Cœna non CORPORALIS, NATURALIS AUT LOCALIS, sive per conversionem totius substantiæ panis & vini, in Corpus & Sanguinem Domini; sive per IMPANATIONEM aut INCLUSIONEM LOCALEM; sive denique per INEXISTENTIAM aut indistántiam, puta Corporalem & Localem: Sed SACRAMENTALIS & SPIRITUALIS est, quam efficit Dei voluntas & Auctoritas, verbis institutionis declarata: pag. 185. init. cæteroquin omni Reali, Spirituali, Supernaturali Cœlestique Corporis Christi veri & substantialis, tam Præsentiæ, quàm Exhibitioni, toto animo subscripturi Auctores dicti.
latin.623: Quoad Præsentiam, credituri & dicturi sincerè cum Irenæo, Cœnam S. duabus rebus, scil. terrenâ & cœlesti constare. Quoad exhibitionem, vel verbis ipsius Prof. Witteberg. VII. citra omnem simulationem, pronunciaturi: Nostri (Reformati) Signa Sacramentalia Exhibitiva nominant non ratione solarum promissionum, usûs & fructûs, sed ratione materiæ, ut loqui amant, cœlestis, seu, quoniam in iis, per elementa externa & visibilia, res cœlestes ac invisibiles, non modò significantur, aut utcunque repræsentantur, sed etiam dispensantur. Quippe quod ipsum non Doctores duntaxat singuli, e. g. Trelcatius, verbis à me in Tractat. Germ. allegatis, sed & Confessiones Reform. publicæ, sigillatim Toruniensis, quæ & Marchica nostraque est, disertissimè enuntiant: Sic enim habet modò dicta Confessio de Cœnâ num. 10. ad num. 13. inclusive: Nequaquam tamen statuimus nuda, vacua, inania Signa, sed potiùs id, quod significant & obsignant, simul, vere exhibentia, tanquam certissima media & efficacia instrumenta, per quæ Corpus & Sanguis Christi, adeoque Christus ipse, cum omnibus suis beneficiis, singulis vescentibus exhibetur, seu offertur, credentibus verò confertur, donatur, & ab ipsis in cibum animæ salutarem & vivificum acceptatur. Nequaquam etiam negamus veram Corporis in Cœna præsentiam, sed tantùm LOCALEM ET CORPORALEM PRÆSENTIÆ MODUM, ET UNIONEM CUM ELEMENTIS SUBSTANTIALIBUS; Ipsam verò nobiscum præsentiam Sanctè credimus & quidem non imaginariam, sed verissimam, realissimam & efficacissimam, nempe ipsam illam Christi nobiscum Unionem mystícám, quam ipsemet ut per verbum promittit, & per Symbola offert, ita per Spiritum efficit, quamque nos per fidem acceptamus, per Charitatem sentimus, secundum vetus illud dictum: Motum sentimus, Modum nescimus, Præsentiam credimus. Unde & patet, non solam virtutem, efficaciam, operationem, aut beneficia Christi nobis præsentari, & communicari, sed imprimis IPSAM SUBSTANTIAM CORPORIS ET SANGUINIS CHRISTI, seu ipsam illam victimam, quæ pro mundi vita data est, & in cruce mactata, ut per fidelem hujus victimæ Communionem, & cum Christo Unionem, consequenter etiam Meritorum & Beneficiorum, Sacrificio ejus partorum, participes simus & sicut ipse in nobis, ita nos in ipso maneamus. Et quidem non tantùm QUOAD ANIMAM, sed etiam QUOAD CORPUS NOSTRUM: Etsi enim ut ore corporis rem terrenam, ita fide cordis, ceu organo proprio, Rem cœlestem acceptamus, secundum veterem illum versiculum: Ventrem, quod terimus, Mentem, quod credimus, intrat tamen, fide illâ mediante, non SOLUM ANIMÆ, sed & IPSA CORPORA, Christi Corpori, per ejusdem Spiritum, ad spem resurrectionis & vitæ æternæ inferuntur & uniuntur, ut simus caro de carne ejus, & os de ossibus ejus, adeóque unum cum ipso Corpus Mysticum, quod Apostolus meritò dicit Mysterium magnum esse.
latin.624: Ex hisce ut spero constabit Clarissimo Viro luculenter satis, Reformatos re verâ credere, non autem simulare se credere, Corpus & Sanguinem Christi verè & substantialiter adesse in Cœna, sicque fatebitur, non modò plurimùm momenti Controversiæ fictitiæ decedere, sed & munitum jam esse aditum ad ea quæ restant partim nullius, partim exigui admodùm momenti, circa fidem Christianam, capita, faciliùs componenda. Horsum etiam pertinent proximæ, quæ adhuc restant, de Cœna secuturæ Protestantium binæ Controversiæ: Una seu Prior, de Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali: De Manducatione Indignorum, altera atque posterior.

pass_a.619: §. XXIV. It is thus proven to the eye that the true and most real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Supper — i.e. the Spiritual — has always been taught and is still today taught by the Reformed Church, derived from Christ Himself the Institutor of the Sacred Supper, through the whole course of Christian ages, as kept and conserved in other Churches, so by order of succession to the Reformed Church; which presence moreover, as antecedent to Faith or spiritual eating, we ourselves have professed with COSIN Bishop of Durham in the little German Tract Kurzer Entwurff p. 64.
pass_a.620: But the truth and evidence of this assertion, firmed and stabilized by as many Reformed testimonies as possible, so lately struck the eyes of a certain most Famous Professor that in a public Disputation on the Supper held by him chamber-fashion last year, in order to prove — by a certainly deplorable attempt — a fundamental Dissension of Protestants in this article, he was not ashamed to write in §. 3 that the Reformeds’ words and external Confessions do not match their Faith — i.e. to use his words: that the Reformed do not really believe what they pretend to believe, and that it is clear to everyone that they feel one thing and speak another. To which most grave injury, so unfairly inflicted on the whole Reformed Church and for so foul and invidious an end, we reply nothing else than the words of his own faithful Preceptor Joh. Conr. Danhauer, by which he defended the Waldenses’ cause in that same case against Joh. Mariana and other Pontiffs — yet to be recited by us without any application to the Professor’s Person: Still in our age, he says, the Pontiffs have dared to write that the Waldenses held Christ’s body not to be in the Eucharist sacrament. They color the matter by another calumny which the Waldenses themselves recount in the Excusing Response to Augustine’s Letters p. 87: They falsely charge us that this is not our Confession, on the ground that we write one thing about the Sacrament of Christ’s Body and believe another. These things being thus premised, Danhauer subjoins what is not alien from this place: For this is the last refuge of those who, if they were otherwise forced to swallow back their calumnies, demand hypocrisy of the adversary without reason; Dissert. on the Waldensian Church art. 4 Phenom. 10 §. 34 in the middle.
pass_a.621: Which things the most Famous Man, to reconcile a certain appearance of injury done to the Reformeds’ company, adduces concerning an intentional and effective presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper remembered by some Reformed; concerning an absence of Christ’s body from the Sacred Supper acknowledged and sincerely professed by others (same §. 4); and fourthly so great a spherical distance of Christ’s Body from the Sacred Supper as the highest Heaven stands from earth, from Calvin, and on denying both illocal and local presence of Christ in the Supper (§. 5 from Trelcatius) — except that (1) these are Comments of private Authors abounding in their own sense, most of them twisted against their mind, as if they were opposed to every real presence of Christ’s body in the Sacred Supper, which yet from their testimonies written into my little Tract stands openly otherwise: Certainly those things strike the Reformed Church no more (even if they were not twisted, having rather suffered something human and adverse to themselves) than the assertions of certain ones commonly coming under the name of Pietists or Syncretists — specially Calixtus, whose Authority the Author himself holds of slight moment among the orthodox (§. 20), as one who played not only with the Reformed but even with the Pontiffs, judged otherwise of the Lutheran Churches’ Symbols, and led some to desert the truth — will be seen to strike the Church which alone the Author holds orthodox and truly Lutheran.
pass_a.622: Also (2) not all things are read in the Authors which the most Famous Man hints stand in them — for example in Trelcatius: ‘that Christ’s body is present on earth neither in a local nor an illocal mode’ does not stand there, seeing that Trelcatius’s words sound thus: For since Christ’s body, homoousion with ours, is in Heaven wherever it wills circumsriptively (namely from the nature of a body, which in a place — i.e. another body — cannot be present otherwise than circumsriptively), not by an invisible uncircumscribed mode (whether absolutely and simply such, or infinite — which is God’s alone — or indefinite / definitive, the essential habit Scholastics give angels) — which modes one and all overturn the truth of a body (as proper and essential adequately either to GOD or to Angels) — it must altogether be confessed that Christ is corporally in Heaven, yet with His Body present in the Supper in a sacramental, i.e. spiritual, mode. pp. 185–186. Also (3) whatever some Authors hand down of intentional or effective presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper; or others of a distance of Christ’s Body from the Supper no less than that between Heaven and earth; or a part of the very absence of Christ’s Body from the Supper; or finally Trelcatius of the circumsriptive mode of Christ’s Body’s presence affirmed in the heavens and the uncircumsriptive mode of being present denied on earth — all that they want opposed only to the corporal, local, and gross mode of Christ’s Body being present in or with or under the Eucharistic bread. For, says Trelcatius: Christ is truly present in the hearts of those who believe, with altogether the same presence as the Communion of His Body is exhibited to them in the Supper. And this presence is REAL, yet neither presence is CORPORAL. For by faith, as Ambrose says, Christ is touched, not by the Body. Leiden ed. p. 184 mid. And a few words later: The mode of the presence of Christ’s Body in the Supper is not CORPORAL, NATURAL OR LOCAL — whether by conversion of the whole substance of bread and wine into the Lord’s Body and Blood; or by IMPANATION or LOCAL INCLUSION; or finally by INEXISTENCE or indistancy, namely Corporal and Local — but is SACRAMENTAL and SPIRITUAL, which God’s will and Authority declared in the Institution words effects (p. 185 beg.). Otherwise the said Authors would with whole mind subscribe to every Real, Spiritual, Supernatural and Heavenly Presence and Exhibition of Christ’s true and substantial Body.
pass_a.623: As to Presence, they would sincerely believe and say with Irenaeus that the Sacred Supper consists of two things, namely earthly and heavenly. As to exhibition, they would pronounce even in the Wittenberg Professor’s own VII words without all pretence: Ours (the Reformed) name the Sacramental Signs Exhibitive not by reason of promises, use and fruit alone, but by reason of the heavenly matter, as they love to speak — or because in them, through external and visible elements, heavenly and invisible things are not only signified or somehow represented but also dispensed. Which very thing not only single Doctors (e.g. Trelcatius in words I alleged in the German Tract) but also the public Reformed Confessions — specially the Torun, which is also our Marchic — most clearly enunciate. For so the said Confession on the Supper holds from n. 10 through n. 13 inclusive: Yet we by no means establish naked, empty, void Signs, but rather ones truly exhibiting at once what they signify and seal, as most certain media and efficacious instruments through which Christ’s Body and Blood — and so Christ Himself with all His benefits — is exhibited or offered to each who eats, but to believers conferred, given, and accepted by them as salutary and life-giving food of the soul. We also by no means deny the true presence of the Body in the Supper, but only the LOCAL AND CORPORAL MODE OF PRESENCE, AND UNION WITH THE SUBSTANTIAL ELEMENTS; but the presence itself with us we believe Holy — and indeed not imaginary, but most true, most real and most efficacious — namely that mystical Union of Christ with us which He Himself as He promises by the word and offers by the Symbols, so effects by the Spirit, and which we accept by faith and feel by Charity, according to that old saying: We feel the motion, we know not the Mode, we believe the Presence. Whence also it is plain that not virtue, efficacy, operation or benefits of Christ alone are presented and communicated to us, but first of all the VERY SUBSTANCE OF CHRIST’S BODY AND BLOOD — or that very victim given for the world’s life and slain on the cross — that through faithful Communion of this victim and Union with Christ we may consequently also be partakers of the Merits and Benefits born of His Sacrifice and as He in us so we may remain in Him. And indeed not only AS TO THE SOUL but also AS TO OUR BODY: for although as with the mouth of the body we accept the earthly thing, so with the heart’s faith as proper organ we accept the heavenly Thing — according to that old little verse: What we rub enters the belly; what we believe, the Mind — yet by that mediating faith not ONLY THE SOULS but also the BODIES THEMSELVES are brought in and united to Christ’s Body by His Spirit unto hope of resurrection and eternal life, that we may be flesh of His flesh and bone of His bones, and so one Mystical Body with Him, which the Apostle rightly says is a great Mystery.
pass_a.624: From these things I hope it will stand lucidly enough to the most Famous Man that the Reformed truly believe — and do not pretend to believe — that Christ’s Body and Blood are truly and substantially present in the Supper; and so he will confess not only that much moment departs from the fictitious Controversy, but also that an approach is already fortified to those remaining heads around the Christian faith of partly no, partly very slight moment, more easily to be composed. Hither also pertain the next two Protestant Controversies on the Supper that still remain to follow: One or the Prior, on the Oral Eating of Christ’s Body; the other and posterior, on the Eating of the Unworthy.

619: §.XXIV: proven to the eye — the true most-real presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Supper is the Spiritual presence the Reformed Church has always taught and still teaches.

It runs from Christ the Institutor through the Christian centuries into the Reformed by succession; and with Cosin (Durham) Strimesius has already professed it as antecedent to faith / spiritual eating (Kurzer Entwurff p. 64).
620: A Clarissimus Professor’s public Supper Disputation lately charged that Reformed confessions do not match their faith — that they feign belief and feel one thing while speaking another (§. 3).

Strimesius answers the grave injury with Danhauer (not applied to the Professor’s person): Pontiffs once said the same of the Waldenses; the Waldenses’ excusing reply and Danhauer call hypocrisy-without-reason the calumniator’s last refuge.
621: The Professor piles intentional/effective presence, some Reformed’s absence-language, Calvin’s heaven–earth distance, and Trelcatius on denying local/illocal presence — as if against every real presence.

Rebuttal (1): mostly private comments twisted against their authors’ mind. Even untwisted they wound the Reformed no more than Pietist/Syncretist (esp. Calixtus) assertions wound the Lutheran church the Professor alone calls orthodox.
622: Rebuttal (2): the alleged Trelcatius line ‘neither local nor illocal on earth’ is not there — Trelcatius says the body is circumsriptively in heaven yet present in the Supper sacramentally / spiritually (pp. 185–186).

Rebuttal (3): all that talk targets only corporal/local/gross presence in/with/under the bread. Trelcatius: the presence is REAL, not CORPORAL (Ambrose: touched by faith, not body); the mode is SACRAMENTAL and SPIRITUAL, not transubstantiation, impanation, or local inclusion — and those authors would subscribe every real spiritual supernatural celestial presence and exhibition.
623: With Irenaeus: Supper = earthly + heavenly. Wittenberg Prof. VII and Torun (Marchic) n.10–13: exhibitiva signs dispense heavenly matter — not naked empty signs; Christ with all benefits offered to every eater, conferred on believers.

They deny only the LOCAL AND CORPORAL mode and substantial union with the elements — and believe the most true mystical union (motion felt, mode unknown, presence believed). What is present is the VERY SUBSTANCE of body and blood (the cross victim), uniting not soul only but our bodies too into one Mystical Body with Christ.
624: §.XXIV close: the Clarissimus Man should now grant the Reformed truly believe — they do not feign — that Christ’s body and blood are truly and substantially present; the fictitious controversy loses much force.
Two Protestant Supper controversies still remain: Prior — Oral Eating of Christ’s Body; Posterior — Eating of the Unworthy. Stop before Annotatio V.
